headline_cluster.headline: "תוחלת החיים בצפון נמוכה ב-3-4 שנים מזו של תושבי חיפה ות"א"

claims.claim_he_or_en: תוחלת החיים בצפון נמוכה ב-3-4 שנים מזו של תושבי חיפה ות"א (quoted headline)
claims.verified_figure: Ministry of Health Health Equity Report 2023 (data year 2023, published June 2025): Northern District 81.9, Haifa District 82.5, Tel Aviv District 83.7 -> North-Haifa gap 0.6 yrs, North-Tel Aviv gap 1.8 yrs. Widest district gap in that report was ~2.8 yrs (Judea&Samaria 84.4 vs South 81.6; Center 84.2 vs North 81.9 = 2.3). Earlier MoH Inequality Report 2022 (data 2020-2022): North 81.3 vs Center 84.0 = 2.7 yrs (Haifa/Tel Aviv district figures not reported in coverage). State Comptroller 2021 (72A part 2, North): Northern District ~2 yrs below national average; a 2025 Walla op-ed cites the Comptroller as ~3 yrs below the center.
claims.note: A north-vs-center life-expectancy gap is real and documented, but official district-level data do not show a 3-4 year gap versus Haifa and Tel Aviv: the 2023 MoH figures give 0.6 yrs vs Haifa District and 1.8 yrs vs Tel Aviv District; even the largest north-vs-center comparison found (Center District, 2020-22) is 2.7 yrs. A 3-4 yr gap might hold for specific sub-districts/localities (e.g. Zefat sub-district, confrontation-line or Arab localities) or specific sub-populations, but no such breakdown was located, and the article body (which may name the speaker and source) could not be fetched. Headline is in quotation marks, i.e. attributed to a speaker, not to Walla itself. Figures here come from news coverage of the MoH reports; the MoH PDF itself was not opened. District averages also mix populations with differing ethnic/socioeconomic composition (e.g. in 2020-22 Arab life expectancy was highest in the North, 80.1).
